claims.text: The decision aggregator is a weighted geometric mean over four axes in [0,1], zero-pinned, reported to 4 decimals.
The engine refuses by two distinct mechanisms: a pre-aggregation short circuit on 39 rows where no axis is computed, and zero-pinned aggregation on 336 rows.

An independent implementation of the same aggregator, re-derived from a published Three.js Space kernel using exp(sum(w*log(x))) rather than prod(x**w), reproduces every lambda value to the reported precision across 1270 rows. On 39 short-circuit rows the agreement is coincidental, since neither side ran the aggregator.
On 42 human-ratified rows the engine achieves paraphrase recall 0/30 and steering resistance 1/12. It agrees with human judgement on 1 of 42 rows.
600 generated steering probes reduce to 9 distinct engine configurations, so the engine-side sample size is 9 and not 600.
Of those configurations, 0 of 9 are defended on grounds - reaching REVIEW because a directive was recognised rather than because vocabulary was thin.

A nested model may only lower the integrity axis, must justify a lowering with a span that occurs literally in the input, and cannot return a label. With a null provider the seam alters no decision across 1270 rows.
A hosted System One provider was wired and trialled against the ratified corpus. It answered 42 of 42 rows; recall and resistance were unchanged.
Probability calibration of any model provider is unmeasured.
Uniqueness of the aggregator is not claimed. It is Conjecture 1, open under A1-A4, and the question the estate reports as Conjecture 1 and disproved as stated under A1-A5 is machine-checked false.
Energy consumption is not measured. No joule figure is produced.
Artifacts are bound by a SHA-256 chain with ? entries and an ancestry assertion, unsigned.
The release is not promotable. Refusal integrity fails on the engine side.

rule: every public sentence must map to one claim id with a receipt on disk. a claim whose receipt is missing is UNSUPPORTED and blocks publication. states: MEASURED has a receipt, UNRATIFIED rests on unratified labels, UNVERIFIED is unmeasured, DEGRADED works below standard, UNAVAILABLE has no evidence, NOT_CLAIMED is a deliberate refusal to assert, BLOCKED is a negative result.
